objective: Revalidate static mesh topology after the owner imposed a symmetric +/-20% vertex budget for the matching original artist attachment.
historicalReview: docs/reviews/GATE_3_2_REVIEW.json retains the previous 3,901-token Jev approval under the superseded one-sided count rule; it cannot unlock Gate 4.
inScope: Read the exact same Spine 4.0.64 attachment and matching PNG to obtain artist total, hull and interior counts
Use those counts to guide deterministic contour simplification and filled cross-section controls without copying artist vertex positions
Before Jev, block each matched case outside its own +/-20% count range; retain separate <=2% corrected foreground missed/added budgets
Compare triangulation and outer/inner point distribution visually against the exact artist JSON, preserving tail regressions
outOfScope: Weights, bones, deformation, head mesh, production art signoff, exact reproduction of artist coordinates
Source art alteration or private PNG, .spine, exported skeleton, mesh coordinates, and comparison images in Git
implementationSummary: MeshGenerationOptions can carry referenceTopology counts from a verified matching attachment. The low curvature contour pass stops near the artist's hull count while retaining simple-polygon, original-edge-distance and separate 2% raster checks. On matched meshes, interior controls are placed at opaque left/right cross-sections derived from the PNG alpha, two per section, up to the reference interior count. They are not sampled from artist vertex coordinates. The independent MeshSpec validator, Earcut, edge improvement and existing geometry paths remain. The reference checker parses the actual exported Spine mesh before generation and passes only its counts. A local hard gate checks signed vertex deviations for required beard and house before SDK load; Jev cannot override a failed count. The tool warns when a generated mesh exceeds the count budget, and always warns deformation is unverified.
humanDecision: User selected +/-20% of each original human attachment and made excessive count deviation disqualifying; topology quality also requires separate review.

Beard triangulation still has four triangles with a minimum angle below 10 degrees, versus none in the artist mesh; animated quality requires later measurement.
The house interior controls follow raster cross-sections and do not reproduce exact artist positions or edge pairings.
